data.title: Benzyl benzoate (25%)
data.summary: Scabicides & pediculicides · Ester of benzyl alcohol and benzoic acid; scabicide
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Scabicides & pediculicides_

**Class:** Ester of benzyl alcohol and benzoic acid; scabicide

## Mechanism of action
- Neurotoxic to mites (kills mites; ovicidal partly)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Scabies (cheap alternative where permethrin is unavailable), pediculosis

## Dose & formulations
- Adults 25% emulsion; dilute to 12.5% for children (and 6% for infants, if used); apply neck down after bath, repeat next day without bathing, wash off 24 h after second application (regimens vary)

## Adverse effects
- Burning and irritation (common, especially on excoriated skin), irritant dermatitis; conjunctivitis if it reaches eyes

## Contraindications
- Infants (irritation, benzyl alcohol toxicity), face and eyes

## Pregnancy & lactation
Has been used; permethrin preferred.

## Viva points
- Burning sensation limits use; must be diluted for children

_Sources: Khopkar ch.21 (Benzyl benzoate); Wolverton 4e ch.44. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
